hints: Focus on the backbone of the chain, remember addition polymers form when a C=C double bond opens to give single C-C links.
Look at the chain in two-carbon sections, you will see a repeating pattern of one $\text{CH}_2$ group next to one $\text{CH(CN)}$ group.
Work backwards by putting the double bond back between those two carbons to rebuild the small alkene that must have joined up.
walkthrough:
**Spot the addition polymer pattern**

Look closely at the long chain. Every carbon is joined by single bonds only, with side groups of H or CN. That tells you it is an addition polymer made from an alkene.

Rule to remember:
$$\text{C=C} \rightarrow \text{-C-C-}$$

**Find the two-carbon repeat unit**

Take the first two carbons on the left. The first is $\text{CH(CN)}$, the second is $\text{CH}_2$. The next two carbons repeat this, $\text{CH(CN)}$ then $\text{CH}_2$, and so on down the chain.

So the repeat unit is:
$$-\text{CH(CN)}-\text{CH}_2-$$

**Rebuild the monomer**

To get the monomer, close the repeat unit back into an alkene by putting the double bond between the two carbons. $\text{CH(CN)}$ becomes $\text{CH(CN)}$ in the alkene and $\text{CH}_2$ stays as $\text{CH}_2$.

Monomer is:
$$\text{CH}_2=\text{CH(CN)}$$

**Match to the options**

$\text{CH}_2=\text{CH(CN)}$ is ethene with one H replaced by one CN group, which is acrylonitrile. That matches the structure with H, H on one carbon and H, CN on the other.

options.A: Correct. This is $\text{CH}_2=\text{CHCN}$. When the C=C opens during addition polymerisation it gives $-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH(CN)}-$, which is exactly the alternating $\text{CH}_2$ and $\text{CH(CN)}$ pattern seen in the chain.
options.B: Incorrect. This is $\text{CH(CN)}=\text{CH(CN)}$, a 1,2-dicyanoethene. It would give two CN groups for every two backbone carbons, but the polymer chain shows only one CN for every two carbons.
options.C: Incorrect. This is a four-carbon diene with two C=C bonds and two CN groups. Dienes give a four-carbon repeat unit and often leave a double bond in the polymer, which does not match this saturated two-carbon repeat.
options.D: Incorrect. This is another four-carbon diene isomer with two CN groups. Like option C, it would produce a longer repeat unit with different CN spacing, not the simple $\text{CH}_2-\text{CH(CN)}$ repeat observed.
